root.input: What is the Standard Traded Player Exception?
root.output:
## The Standard Traded Player Exception

Under **Art. VII §6(j)(1)(i)**, the Standard Traded Player Exception lets a Team that trades away one player ("Traded Player") acquire one or more "Replacement Players" to take his place, subject to a salary-matching cap:

- The Replacement Player(s)' combined post-assignment Salary (for the Salary Cap Year in which they're acquired) can be no more than **100% of the Traded Player's pre-trade Salary, plus $250,000**.
- Replacement Players can be acquired **simultaneously or non-simultaneously** with the trade — but any non-simultaneous acquisition must happen **within one year** of the date the Traded Player was traded.
- It is subject to the broader rules in Art. VII §2(e) (hard-cap/apron rules) and §6(n) and §6(j)(6).

Two related wrinkles from the same section:
- **§6(j)(3):** If the trading Team's post-assignment Apron Team Salary would exceed the First Apron Level, the $250,000 allowance drops to **$0**.
- This exception is distinct from its siblings in the same subsection — the Aggregated (§6(j)(1)(ii)), Transition (§6(j)(1)(iii), 2023-24 only), Expanded (§6(j)(1)(iv)), and Room Under Cap Plus $250,000 (§6(j)(1)(v)) exceptions — which use different matching percentages or apply to multiple Traded Players at once.

Separately, **Art. VII §8** ("Trade Rules") governs the broader mechanics of trades generally (cash limits, no-trade consent windows, timing restrictions after signing, etc.) but does not itself define the Standard Traded Player Exception — that definition lives solely in §6(j)(1)(i).

root.name: answer-cba-question
root.input: A team sends out $30,000,000 in salary. How much can it take back?
root.output:
Under the **Standard Traded Player Exception** (Art. VII §6(j)(1)(i)), a team sending out salary can take back **up to 100% of the outgoing player's pre-trade Salary, plus $250,000** — i.e., on $30,000,000 outgoing, the incoming replacement player(s)' aggregate post-assignment Salary may be no more than 100% of that $30,000,000 figure plus $250,000.

Two important caveats from the same Article:

- **Apron limit (Art. VII §6(j)(3)):** if the team's post-assignment Apron Team Salary would exceed the First Apron Level, the $250,000 allowance is reduced to **$0** — so the ceiling becomes exactly 100% of the outgoing salary, no cushion.
- **Cash limit (Art. VII §8(a)):** separately, any cash received in trades (not salary-matching) is capped at **5.15% of the Salary Cap** for the Salary Cap Year, aggregated across all trades in that year.

I haven't computed the dollar result of applying 100% + $250,000 (or the apron-reduced version) — that arithmetic is for query_league_data if you want the exact figure, and it would also require knowing whether the team is above the First Apron.
